name: PageGrid
summary: A page's composition grid (DesignUp, owner 2026-11-12 23:54, 2026-11-13 02:27): the page is rows; a row's cells divide its span of the page's twelve columns (`span`, at least 3 where a row has more than one cell, so at most four across); a cell holds more rows or is a slot for one block or fundamental. Spans are absolute at every depth, so a nested row only subdivides its parent's span and every cell lines up with the page's columns. An empty slot keeps its size (`data-empty`, setting `--c-page-grid-empty-size`), so a preview lays out as the editor does. The edits an editor makes (split in two, merge two empty cells, move a border, add a row) are `@design-library/core/page-grid`. Rows sit a chosen stack step apart (`gap`); columns a fixed gutter apart. A row whose narrowest cell would be under `size.column-min` stacks its cells in source order, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px. The only way to put blocks side by side on a page: blocks never nest a page inside themselves. Not for things compared side by side inside a block (use Grid), an app's regions (use AppLayout or EditorLayout) or free positioning (there is none).
a11y: Plain `div`s with no role: the grid arranges, it doesn't group. Reading order is the source order, row by row and cell by cell, at every width. Pointer selection (`onSelect`) is an editor's shortcut; its keyboard path is the editor's outline of the same rows and cells (a TreeView), which sets `selected`.

props.name: rows
props.description: The page's rows, top to bottom. Each row splits into cells; a cell holds rows or is a slot.

props.name: renderSlot
props.description: Fills a slot (a cell without rows) with one block or one fundamental; return nothing to leave it empty.

props.name: selected
props.description: The id of the row or cell an editor has selected: it carries the selection outline (`data-selected`).

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Makes rows and cells selectable by pointer, for an editor: a click picks the innermost cell under it, or its row where no cell is (between cells). Keyboard selection belongs to the editor's outline (a TreeView of the same ids).

props.name: start
props.description: The space above the first row (LR91): a stack step, as a row's `gap`; none by default.

props.name: end
props.description: The space below the last row (LR91); none by default.

props.name: layoutEdges
props.description: The grid sits in a gap-free group with its neighbouring regions of a SiteLayout column (Stack gap="none", LR127): a named `start` or `end` then also carries the column's gap, so it measures as before, and none is exactly 0. Off by default.

props.name: id
props.description: Stable id: the key, and `data-cell` on the cell for an editor to find it.

props.name: span
props.description: The page columns the cell spans (absolute at every depth, at least 3 of 12 where a row has more than one cell); a row's spans add up to its span. A row of one cell may leave it out (the whole span).

props.name: rows
props.description: Rows inside the cell, each dividing the cell's span again. Without rows the cell is a slot: `renderSlot` fills it.

props.name: id
props.description: Stable id: the key, and `data-row` on the row.

props.name: split
props.description: @deprecated Give the cells `span`s. A preset division of the row's span, still read.

props.name: gap
props.description: The space above the row; the first row of a group has none (default `section`; `none` is exactly 0, LR127).

props.name: cells
props.description: The row's cells in reading order.

settings.description: The least height of an empty cell (default 0: an empty cell takes no height). An editor's preview sets the height its canvas gives an empty cell, so a page previews with the layout it's edited in.
